### Q5. A healthcare worker finds an adult unresponsive with absent normal breathing and no definite pulse after a check lasting no more than 10 seconds. What should happen next?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Observe for five minutes before initiating CPR
- **B.** Activate emergency response, start CPR and obtain an AED
- **C.** Start rescue breathing alone indefinitely
- **D.** Give oral water while waiting

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Activate emergency response, start CPR and obtain an AED**

Cardiac arrest ka matlab hai heart body ko effective blood circulation nahi de pa raha hai. Agar adult unresponsive hai, normal breathing nahi hai aur trained healthcare worker ko 10 seconds ke andar definite pulse nahi milti, toh cardiac arrest assume karo. Emergency system activate karo, chest compressions shuru karo aur AED mangwao. AED ek device hai jo rhythm analyse karke zaroorat hone par shock advise karta hai. Trained team ventilation bhi provide karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Paanch minute observe karne se circulation restore karne ka precious time waste hota hai.
- **B (Sahi):** CPR aur emergency response se brain aur heart ko blood supply milne ka chance improve hota hai. AED jaldi available hona bhi important hai.
- **C (Galat):** Rescue breathing alone definite pulse hone par respiratory arrest ke liye useful ho sakti hai. Pulseless arrest mein compressions zaroori hain.
- **D (Galat):** Unresponsive patient safely swallow nahi kar sakta. Water airway mein ja sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** No definite pulse within 10 seconds with absent normal breathing = start CPR.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q40. During adult CPR before placement of an advanced airway, what compression-to-ventilation ratio is generally used by trained healthcare providers?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** 30:2
- **B.** 15:2
- **C.** 3:1
- **D.** 5:1

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. 30:2**

Adult cardiac arrest mein trained rescuer advanced airway placement se pehle 30 chest compressions ke baad 2 breaths deta hai. Breaths se visible chest rise hona chahiye, excessive ventilation nahi. Is ratio se circulation aur oxygenation dono support hote hain. Advanced airway lagne ke baad trained team continuous compressions aur asynchronous ventilation ka protocol follow kar sakti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** 30:2 conventional adult CPR before advanced airway ka standard ratio hai.
- **B (Galat):** 15:2 two-rescuer pediatric CPR ke selected situations mein use hota hai, routine adult CPR mein nahi.
- **C (Galat):** 3:1 birth ke samay selected neonatal resuscitation ka ratio hai. Yeh routine adult CPR ka ratio nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** 5:1 current conventional adult CPR ka standard ratio nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Adult pre-advanced airway: 30:2. Two-rescuer pediatric: 15:2.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

**Related tested concept:** [AIIMS NORCET 6 Prelims 2024 — third-party memory-based report](https://testbook.com/question-answer/normal-compression-to-ventilation-ratio--662a417c532eac8383c8778d). Retrieved source reports adult 30:2 ratio. Original official paper and key not authenticated. This bank item is original.

### Q53. Which chest compression rate is recommended for adult CPR under the AHA 2025 guidance?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** 100–120/min
- **B.** 60–80/min
- **C.** 40–60/min
- **D.** 140–160/min

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. 100–120/min**

Chest compression mein sternum ko rhythmically press karke heart se blood flow support kiya jaata hai. AHA 2025 adult CPR ke liye 100–120 compressions per minute ka target rakhti hai. Rate ke saath proper depth, full chest recoil aur chhoti interruptions bhi zaroori hain. Sirf fast compressions karne se quality automatically achhi nahi hoti.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** 100–120/min adult CPR ka recommended range hai. Depth aur recoil bhi maintain karo.
- **B (Galat):** 60–80/min recommended adult CPR rate se kam hai. Isse per minute compressions kam ho sakti hain.
- **C (Galat):** 40–60/min adult CPR ke liye bahut slow hai aur adequate circulation support nahi kar sakta.
- **D (Galat):** 140–160/min recommended upper range se zyada hai. Itni speed par adequate depth aur recoil maintain karna mushkil ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Adult CPR: 100–120/min, full recoil.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q61. What is the recommended manual chest compression depth for an average adult during CPR?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** About 5–6 cm
- **B.** About 7–9 cm
- **C.** Only 1 cm
- **D.** About 2–3 cm

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. About 5–6 cm**

Compression depth batati hai chest ko kitna neeche press karna hai. Average adult mein at least 5 cm depth target hoti hai aur 6 cm se zyada excessive compression avoid karni chahiye. Adequate depth blood flow support karti hai. Rescuer ko firm support aur correct hand position ke saath quality monitor karni chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Approximately 5–6 cm adult depth recommended range ko represent karti hai.
- **B (Galat):** 7–9 cm recommended adult depth se zyada hai aur unnecessary trauma ka risk badha sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** 1 cm compression average adult mein effective circulation ke liye insufficient hai.
- **D (Galat):** 2–3 cm usual adult target se kam hai. Is depth par blood flow inadequate ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Adult depth 5–6 cm. Pediatric depth rules alag hain.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q38. An AED announces that a shock is advised. Which action is correct?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Wait several minutes after shock before resuming compressions
- **B.** Delay shock until a complete clinical history is obtained
- **C.** Keep a hand on the patient during shock
- **D.** Ensure no one is touching the patient, deliver the shock as directed and resume CPR promptly

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Ensure no one is touching the patient, deliver the shock as directed and resume CPR promptly**

AED rhythm analyse karke shockable rhythm mein shock advise karta hai. Shock se pehle sabko patient se contact hatana chahiye, aur device prompts follow karne chahiye. Shock ke turant baad usual algorithm mein chest compressions resume hoti hain, jab tak clear signs ya team assessment se circulation return ka indication na ho. Long unnecessary pause se perfusion gir sakti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Shock ke baad minutes tak wait karna CPR interruption ko badha deta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Complete history ka wait indicated shock ko unnecessarily delay karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Shock ke waqt patient ko touch karna rescuer safety risk create karta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Clear contact, deliver advised shock, then promptly resume CPR according to device and team protocol.

**Exam clue:** AED: clear, shock if advised, resume CPR promptly.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q58. Why should rescuers allow complete chest recoil between compressions?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Recoil is needed only after defibrillation
- **B.** Recoil supports venous return and cardiac filling
- **C.** Recoil prevents the heart from receiving blood
- **D.** Continuous leaning increases ventricular filling

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Recoil supports venous return and cardiac filling**

Recoil ka matlab har compression ke baad chest ko apni normal position mein poora wapas aane dena hai. Jab chest release hoti hai toh venous blood ko heart ki taraf return karne ka mauka milta hai. Agar rescuer chest par leaned rehta hai toh filling aur circulation compromise ho sakti hai. Hands ko position par rakho lekin residual pressure release karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Recoil har compression cycle ka part hai. Defibrillation ke baad hi zaroori nahi hota.
- **B (Sahi):** Complete recoil heart filling aur agle compression ke liye blood flow support karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Recoil heart ko blood receive karne se nahi rokta. Yeh filling support karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Leaning intrathoracic pressure ko elevated rakh sakti hai aur venous return impair kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Press, release fully, avoid leaning.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q95. An adult is unresponsive and makes occasional gasping sounds. How should a trained responder interpret gasping?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** It proves spontaneous circulation has returned
- **B.** It establishes effective normal breathing
- **C.** It is abnormal breathing that can occur during cardiac arrest
- **D.** It excludes the need for emergency assessment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. It is abnormal breathing that can occur during cardiac arrest**

Agonal gasping mein patient occasional irregular gasps le sakta hai, lekin yeh effective normal ventilation nahi hoti. Cardiac arrest ke early phase mein gasps present ho sakte hain. Healthcare worker responsiveness, breathing aur pulse ko rapidly assess karta hai. Definite pulse 10 seconds ke andar feel na ho toh CPR start karna chahiye. Lay rescuer normal breathing absent hone par emergency dispatcher guidance follow kare.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Gasping se return of spontaneous circulation prove nahi hota. Iske liye clinical assessment chahiye.
- **B (Galat):** Occasional gasps effective normal breathing establish nahi karte.
- **C (Sahi):** Gasping abnormal breathing hai aur cardiac arrest mein ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Gasping serious emergency ka sign ho sakti hai. Assessment skip nahi karna chahiye.

**Exam clue:** Agonal gasps are not normal breathing.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q115. When two trained rescuers are available, how often should the chest compressor generally change during adult CPR?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Approximately every two minutes or sooner if fatigued
- **B.** Only when the patient regains consciousness
- **C.** Only every ten minutes
- **D.** After every single compression

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Approximately every two minutes or sooner if fatigued**

Repeated chest compressions physically tiring hoti hain. Rescuer fatigue hone par compressions shallow ya irregular ho sakti hain, kabhi fatigue notice hone se pehle bhi. Do trained rescuers available hon toh approximately har 2 minutes mein compressor change karo, ya fatigue hone par pehle. Switch ko rhythm analysis ya planned brief pause ke saath coordinate karo taaki interruption minimum ho.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Around two-minute rotation compression quality maintain karne mein help karti hai. Fatigue pehle ho toh sooner switch appropriate hai.
- **B (Galat):** Consciousness return ka wait karna rotation ka criterion nahi hai. CPR quality abhi maintain karni hai.
- **C (Galat):** Ten minutes tak same compressor rakhne se fatigue ke karan quality decline ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Har single compression ke baad switch karne se unnecessary interruptions aur coordination problem hongi.

**Exam clue:** Switch compressor about every 2 minutes, with minimal interruption.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q4. A patient has a deeply embedded object in a wound. Which first aid approach is safest?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Push it deeper to stop movement
- **B.** Apply direct pressure on its protruding end
- **C.** Pull the object out immediately
- **D.** Stabilize the object, control bleeding around it and obtain urgent help

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Stabilize the object, control bleeding around it and obtain urgent help**

Deeply embedded object wound ke andar injured tissue ya blood vessel ke against pressure bana raha ho sakta hai. Field mein object nikalne se bleeding ya injury suddenly worsen ho sakti hai. Object ko movement se protect karo, bleeding ke liye suitable pressure uske aas-paas do, protruding object par nahi. Urgent clinical care arrange karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Object deeper push karne se blood vessels, nerves aur tissues ko further injury ho sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Protruding end par pressure object ko andar move kar sakta hai aur injury worsen kar sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Object pull karne se clot ya injured vessel disturb ho sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Object stabilize karke around-wound bleeding control aur urgent help safest listed action hai.

**Exam clue:** Embedded object: do not remove or press on it. Stabilize and escalate.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q44. An adult with severe choking becomes unresponsive. What is the appropriate transition?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Activate emergency help and begin CPR, checking for a visible object before breaths
- **B.** Continue standing abdominal thrusts indefinitely
- **C.** Wait for spontaneous coughing before taking action
- **D.** Perform blind finger sweeps after every compression

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Activate emergency help and begin CPR, checking for a visible object before breaths**

Jab severe choking wala adult unresponsive ho jaata hai toh emergency response activate karo agar pehle nahi kiya. Safe surface par chest compressions se CPR begin karo. Jab airway breaths dene ke liye open karo toh visible foreign body ko remove karo. Agar object visible nahi hai toh finger blindly andar mat daalo. Team ya dispatcher algorithm follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Unresponsive choking mein CPR start karna aur visible object check karna recommended transition hai.
- **B (Galat):** Unresponsive patient ko standing position mein abdominal thrusts dete rehna appropriate nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Spontaneous cough ka wait airway obstruction aur oxygen deprivation ko prolong karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Blind sweep se object deeper push ho sakta hai. Sirf clearly visible object remove karo.

**Exam clue:** Unresponsive choking: CPR starting with compressions. Visible object only.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q82. Which first aid action is appropriate for significant external bleeding from a limb?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Wash the wound continuously instead of controlling bleeding
- **B.** Raise the limb only and ignore ongoing bleeding
- **C.** Apply firm direct pressure using suitable dressing and activate help
- **D.** Remove the developing clot repeatedly

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Apply firm direct pressure using suitable dressing and activate help**

External bleeding mein blood body se bahar nikal raha hota hai. Significant limb bleeding mein suitable dressing ke saath firm direct pressure lagane se injured vessel se blood loss kam ho sakta hai. Emergency help activate karo aur available PPE use karo. Life-threatening limb bleeding mein direct pressure ineffective ya impractical ho toh trained provider appropriate tourniquet use kar sakta hai. Shock signs aur ongoing bleeding monitor karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Washing alone significant bleeding stop nahi karti. Pehle hemorrhage control priority hai.
- **B (Galat):** Elevation alone persistent major bleeding ke liye adequate treatment nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Direct pressure bleeding control ka basic intervention hai. Significant blood loss mein urgent help bhi zaroori hai.
- **D (Galat):** Forming clot baar-baar remove karne se bleeding restart ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Bleeding control: direct pressure and urgent escalation. Tourniquet for indicated severe limb bleeding.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

### Q108. A conscious adult cannot speak or cough effectively because of severe foreign-body airway obstruction. Which sequence is recommended in AHA 2025 adult guidance?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Blind finger sweeps repeated until relief
- **B.** Give water to wash the obstruction down
- **C.** Begin routine chest compressions while the patient remains responsive
- **D.** Cycles of five back blows followed by five abdominal thrusts

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Cycles of five back blows followed by five abdominal thrusts**

Severe foreign-body airway obstruction ka matlab hai object airflow ko itna block kar raha hai ki patient effective cough, bolna ya saans lena nahi kar pa raha. Emergency help activate karo. AHA 2025 conscious adult mein 5 back blows aur phir 5 abdominal thrusts ke repeated cycles recommend karti hai. Late pregnancy ya abdomen encircle na kar paane par abdominal thrusts ki jagah chest thrusts use hoti hain. Effective cough wale mild obstruction mein cough encourage karo aur monitor karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Blind finger sweep object ko aur andar dhakel sakta hai aur trauma kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Water dena airway mein ja sakta hai aur obstruction treat nahi karta.
- **C (Galat):** Responsive choking adult mein routine CPR compressions pehla step nahi hain. Unresponsive ho jaaye toh CPR transition hoti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Five back blows followed by five abdominal thrusts 2025 AHA conscious severe adult choking sequence hai.

**Exam clue:** 2025 update: 5 back blows + 5 abdominal thrusts, not older thrust-only teaching.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support)

### Q26. A patient has a convulsive seizure in bed. Which action is appropriate during the event?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Protect from injury, time the seizure and assess airway and breathing
- **B.** Give oral tablets during active convulsions
- **C.** Restrain the limbs tightly
- **D.** Force a spoon between the teeth

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Protect from injury, time the seizure and assess airway and breathing**

Convulsive seizure mein brain ki abnormal electrical activity ke karan involuntary movements ho sakti hain. Patient ke aas-paas hazards remove karo, head protect karo aur seizure ka time note karo. Breathing assess karo aur safe ho toh seizure ke baad side positioning consider karo. Patient ko restrain mat karo aur mouth mein object mat daalo. First seizure, 5 minutes se lamba seizure, repeated seizures without recovery ya breathing problem urgent emergency help maangte hain. In-hospital escalation protocol follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Injury prevention, timing aur airway-breathing assessment seizure first aid ke central actions hain.
- **B (Galat):** Active convulsions mein oral tablets aspiration ya choking ka risk create karti hain.
- **C (Galat):** Limbs tightly restrain karne se muscle, joint aur soft-tissue injury ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Spoon teeth ke beech force karne se dental injury, airway obstruction aur rescuer injury ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Protect, time, assess breathing. Nothing forced into mouth.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q46. A person collapses following electrical contact. What must a responder ensure before touching the person?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Water is poured over the electrical device
- **B.** The electrical source has been safely isolated
- **C.** The person is lifted while still contacting the live source
- **D.** The person is dragged away with bare wet hands

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. The electrical source has been safely isolated**

Electrical injury mein patient live source ke contact mein ho toh rescuer bhi current ke path ka part ban sakta hai. Pehle scene safety ensure karo aur source ko safely isolate karwao. High-voltage scene mein trained emergency personnel ke clearance ke bina approach mat karo. Scene safe hone ke baad responsiveness, breathing, circulation aur injuries assess karo. Collapse mein BLS aur emergency response as indicated shuru karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Live electrical equipment par water pour karna conduction aur shock hazard badha sakta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Safe power isolation rescuer aur patient dono ko continued electrical exposure se protect karti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Live contact ke dauran person ko touch ya lift karna rescuer ko bhi shock de sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Wet bare hands se direct contact electrical shock ka serious risk hai.

**Exam clue:** Electrical injury: scene safe before patient contact.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/first-aid/performing-first-aid/first-aid-steps) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/burns)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q97. An alert patient with a suspected limb fracture awaits emergency assessment. Which first aid principle is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Support the injured limb in its found position and avoid unnecessary movement
- **B.** Massage the fracture site vigorously
- **C.** Force the limb straight regardless of pain
- **D.** Ask the patient to bear weight to test the injury

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Support the injured limb in its found position and avoid unnecessary movement**

Fracture bone ke break ya crack ko kehte hain. Suspected fracture mein movement se pain, bleeding aur surrounding nerve-vessel injury worsen ho sakti hai. Limb ko found position mein support karo aur unnecessary movement avoid karo. Distal color, warmth, sensation aur circulation assess karo. Severe bleeding, absent distal circulation ya open fracture urgent professional care maangte hain. Forceful realignment routine first aid nahi hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Found position mein support movement-related harm ko reduce karta hai jab trained help ka wait ho.
- **B (Galat):** Vigorous massage fracture site ko stabilize nahi karti aur bleeding/pain worsen kar sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Force se limb straight karne se displaced bone nearby tissue injure kar sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Weight-bearing test suspected fracture mein displacement ya further injury kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Support as found, check distal circulation, arrange assessment.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/fractures)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q115. What is appropriate immediate first aid for a small recent thermal burn when safe water is available?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Apply toothpaste to the injured skin
- **B.** Apply ice directly for a prolonged period
- **C.** Break all blisters immediately
- **D.** Cool the burn with cool running water and avoid ice

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Cool the burn with cool running water and avoid ice**

Thermal burn heat ke karan skin injury hai. Small recent burn mein cool clean running water heat ko remove karne aur ongoing tissue damage limit karne mein help karti hai. Cooling ke dauran baaki body ko warm rakho. Loose jewelry ko swelling se pehle hatao agar safely possible ho. Large, deep, electrical, special-site ya inhalation-risk burn mein urgent clinical assessment chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Toothpaste burn treatment nahi hai. Isse contamination aur assessment difficulty ho sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Ice directly skin par lagane se cold injury ho sakti hai aur tissue damage badh sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Blister skin ko protective covering provide kar sakta hai. Routine breaking se infection risk badh sakta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Cool running water immediate suitable cooling method hai. Direct ice avoid karo.

**Exam clue:** Cool the burn, not the whole patient. Do not use ice or toothpaste.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines) · [Clinical reference 2](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/burns)

### Q4. A person with a suspected venomous snakebite is waiting for transport. Which first aid principle is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Cut the wound and suck out venom
- **B.** Apply ice and a tightly occlusive arterial tourniquet
- **C.** Encourage running to the hospital
- **D.** Keep the person calm, minimize limb movement and arrange urgent hospital transport

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Keep the person calm, minimize limb movement and arrange urgent hospital transport**

Suspected venomous snakebite mein venom body mein spread ho sakta hai. Patient ko reassure karo, unnecessary movement avoid karo aur bitten limb ko gently immobilize karke urgent hospital transport arrange karo. Rings ya tight items safely remove karo agar swelling ka risk ho. Airway aur breathing monitor karo. Tight arterial tourniquet, cutting, suction aur ice se harm ho sakta hai. Pressure-immobilization technique ko har snakebite par apply nahi karna chahiye. Local Indian guideline aur trained advice follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Wound cutting aur suction venom ka reliable removal nahi karte aur tissue injury/infection risk badha sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Tight tourniquet circulation block karke tissue injury kar sakta hai. Ice bhi local injury worsen kar sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Running se muscle movement badhegi aur safe transport delay ho sakta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Calm reassurance, immobilization aur rapid transport WHO first-aid principle ke consistent hain.

**Exam clue:** Snakebite: immobilize and transport, no cutting or tight tourniquet.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://www.who.int/teams/control-of-neglected-tropical-diseases/snakebite-envenoming/treatment)

### Q15. A patient develops severe wheezing and hypotension after an allergen exposure. What is the priority under anaphylaxis protocol?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Allow the patient to stand and walk alone
- **B.** Activate emergency help and give indicated intramuscular epinephrine promptly under protocol
- **C.** Wait for oral antihistamine to work before escalation
- **D.** Give water as the sole treatment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Activate emergency help and give indicated intramuscular epinephrine promptly under protocol**

Anaphylaxis severe allergic reaction hai jisme airway swelling, bronchospasm aur blood pressure girna rapidly develop ho sakta hai. IM epinephrine, jise adrenaline bhi kehte hain, first-line treatment hai. Emergency team activate karo aur indicated protocol ke mutabik IM dose anterolateral thigh mein do. Breathing aur circulation support aur reassessment zaroori hai. Patient ko suddenly stand ya walk mat karwao. Position breathing aur circulation ki condition ke hisaab se decide karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Hypotension mein standing ya walking circulation collapse ka risk badha sakti hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Prompt indicated IM epinephrine aur emergency escalation airway aur circulatory compromise address karne ki priority hai.
- **C (Galat):** Antihistamines skin symptoms mein help kar sakti hain, lekin shock ya airway obstruction ke liye epinephrine replace nahi karti.
- **D (Galat):** Water anaphylactic shock ya airway swelling ka effective treatment nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine first, not antihistamine first.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q49. A hypoglycemic patient is unconscious and cannot swallow safely. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Pour sweet liquid into the patient's mouth
- **B.** Wait until the patient becomes alert without monitoring
- **C.** Activate urgent help and administer prescribed emergency treatment by a safe nonoral route
- **D.** Force the patient to swallow tablets

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Activate urgent help and administer prescribed emergency treatment by a safe nonoral route**

Severe hypoglycemia brain function disturb kar sakti hai aur patient unconscious ho sakta hai. Unconscious patient ke protective swallowing reflexes reliable nahi hote. Isliye oral glucose mat do. Urgent help activate karo, airway aur breathing assess karo aur authorized protocol ke mutabik IV glucose ya glucagon jaise safe nonoral treatment arrange karo. Repeat glucose aur clinical response monitor karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Sweet liquid mouth mein pour karne se aspiration ho sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Bina treatment aur monitoring wait karna severe hypoglycemia ko prolong karta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Urgent help aur appropriate nonoral glucose-raising treatment safe priority hai.
- **D (Galat):** Tablet force karne se airway obstruction aur aspiration ka risk hai.

**Exam clue:** Unsafe swallow = no oral glucose. Escalate and follow emergency protocol.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S339/163925/16-Diabetes-Care-in-the-Hospital-Standards-of-Care) · [Clinical reference 2](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q83. An adult with diabetes is alert, has low measured glucose and can swallow safely. Which initial response is commonly appropriate under a hypoglycemia protocol?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Withhold carbohydrate until loss of consciousness
- **B.** Give a large high-fat meal as the only rapid intervention
- **C.** Give additional insulin immediately
- **D.** Give a measured fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose at the specified interval

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Give a measured fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose at the specified interval**

Hypoglycemia ka matlab blood glucose low hona hai. Alert adult jo safely swallow kar sakta hai aur oral intake allowed hai, usko protocol ke according fast-acting glucose do. Common adult plan mein 15 g fast carbohydrate aur 15 minutes baad repeat glucose check hota hai. Agar low rahe toh protocol ke hisaab se repeat treatment aur escalation karo. Individual dose aur monitoring situation ke according vary kar sakte hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Consciousness lose hone ka wait serious neurological harm ka risk badhata hai.
- **B (Galat):** High-fat meal ka absorption slow ho sakta hai. Yeh initial rapid glucose correction ka suitable substitute nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Additional insulin blood glucose aur kam kar sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Measured fast carbohydrate glucose ko quickly raise karne mein help karti hai. Repeat monitoring treatment effect confirm karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Alert and safe swallow: fast glucose, recheck per protocol.

**Clinical references:** [Clinical reference 1](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S132/163927/6-Glycemic-Goals-Hypoglycemia-and-Hyperglycemic) · [Clinical reference 2](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S339/163925/16-Diabetes-Care-in-the-Hospital-Standards-of-Care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>
